sections.content: How many people stayed in Castle Donington after gaining qualifications?

Castle Donington is a small town in the East Midlands. Castle Donington does not have its own university.

Castle Donington has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Castle Donington ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 270 state-school pupils from Castle Donington who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 90 (33%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 80 (30%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Castle Donington to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Castle Donington's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Castle Donington in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

In 2018 to 2019, 44% of graduates and 47% of qualified non-graduates living in Castle Donington had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 90 graduates and 95 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Castle Donington. This is compared with the 90 graduates and 80 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 56% of the graduates had also lived in Castle Donington as GCSE pupils, while 44% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Castle Donington in 2018 to 2019, 53% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 47% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
